one_month_reasoning: Arista's Q3 2026 report is expected around Nov 2-3, 2026, i.e. just after the Oct 30 window, so no company print falls inside it (the date announcement itself, likely early October, is not a price event). The main scheduled in-window events are hyperscaler Q3 reports in the last week of October (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon) whose 2027 capex commentary is the single biggest read-through for ANET (Meta and Microsoft were 26% and 16% of FY2025 revenue); these could move the stock 5-10% either way but I have no edge on sign. Stock is near its 52-week high after a ~+80% run from the low, with steady 10b5-1 insider selling; I take only a very slight negative tilt (median ~$203) and use monthly vol ~15.5% (54%/3.5), i.e. near-symmetric.

bear.story: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth decelerates or a top customer (Meta/Microsoft, 42% of FY25 revenue) pauses; Nvidia Spectrum-X bundling keeps taking share (IDC: 21.5% vs Arista 20.7% in 1Q26); gross margin slides toward 60% on mix and memory costs; $9.7B purchase commitments become an inventory overhang. 2027 EPS ~$4.3 at 25-27x plus cash.

base.story: Revenue grows ~20-25% in 2027 to ~$15.5B, margins stable around 62-63% gross / 47-48% operating, EPS ~$5.0; multiple compresses from ~50x to ~35x forward, roughly offsetting earnings growth.

bull.story: AI back-end and scale-across networks plus front-end/campus keep 2027 growth near 30%, EPS ~$5.6-6.0 and 2028 visibility supports ~45x; Nvidia share gains prove to be mostly incremental market growth.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$140 (about -31%, under the post-Q1 selloff low near $149) the stock would likely be pricing a guidance cut, a major hyperscaler pause or clear share loss to Nvidia/white box rather than multiple noise; at that level the ~$9.7B non-cancellable purchase commitments and deferred-revenue build would turn from a support into an inventory/write-down risk.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Fundamentals are excellent and there is no accounting, credit or litigation red flag: 10-Q shows $13.3B cash/securities, no debt, litigation provisions 'not significant', OCF $2.78B in H1. The bear case is therefore about expectations, not solvency: (1) valuation ~50x 2026 EPS (~$4.08 run-rate) and ~41x my 2027 estimate (~$5.00); (2) concentration: two customers were 26% and 16% of FY25 revenue; (3) Nvidia overtook Arista in data-center Ethernet switching in 1Q26 per IDC; (4) gross margin down ~230bp y/y to 62.9% GAAP, with management absorbing memory costs; (5) non-cancellable purchase commitments of $9.7B (~75% of 2026 revenue) and deferred revenue up $1.5B in H1 amplify a downturn if orders pause; (6) AI capex growth is forecast to decelerate from ~100% (2026) to ~54% (2027) and ~12% (2028), so by Sep-2027 the market will be pricing a slowdown year; (7) sustained 10b5-1 insider selling (~$746M in 90 days per MarketBeat) is informative only weakly. Against that, guidance was raised three times in 2026 and consensus is 23 Buys. My fair value ~$193 sits a bit below spot. The ladder is a three-component lognormal mixture (bear $125/25%, base $205/50%, bull $290/25%), giving median ~$204, mean ~$210, and a fat left tail consistent with 54% realized vol; this is a slight downside skew versus a pure drift model.
